High yielding milch animals in
backward regions
*21. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANW ARA
TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL
DARDA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Chairperson of
National Dairy Development Board
(NDDB) has stated that it is futile to
provide high-yielding milch animals in the
backward districts where infrastructure is
lacking and which have no marketing
scope;
(b) if so, whether Government is aware
that a tribal district V alsad has made
phenomenal progress in milk production
inspite of opinion of National Dairy
Development Programme (NDDP) in 1975-
76 that dairy activities there were
impossible due to its location, illiterate tribal
people and shortage of water, etc., and
(c) whether NDDP would penetrate
deep in Vidarbha to diversify farm-related
activities in this tribal region?
RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, November 20, 2009/Kartika 29, 1931 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Human Resource Development; Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
Effecting ban on Endosulfan
†*22. SHRI SATY A VRAT
CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the pesticide
endosulfan is banned in 62 countries and a
demand is being made for several years to
ban this in India too;
(b) whether it is also a fact that several
hormonal and re-productivity related
defects are developing due to this
pesticide;
(c) whether it is also a fact that it was
extensively used in tea gardens before 2003
due to which people suffered with fatal
diseases;
(d) if so, the reasons for not banning
such type of dangerous pesticide in India;
and
(e) by when a ban would be put on
it?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

9
Financial assistance to drought
affected States
*23. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY :
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether in the wake of drought in
major parts of the country, the food subsidy
extended by the Central Government to
States, has risen to Rs. 61,000 crores from
Rs. 42,000 crores in 2008-09;
(b) whether his Ministry has already
sent teams of experts to all 12 affected States
in the month of August and the teams have
already submitted their assessment;
(c) if so, whether affected States have
released a sum of Rs. 1600 crores without
going into the feedback reports; and
(d) if so, to what extent the financial
help provided to the States has helped in
tackling the drought in the States?
Ceiling on BPL beneficiaries under
National Food Security Bill
*24. SHRI A. ELA V ARASAN: Will the
Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has requested
State Governments to put a ceiling on the
number of BPL beneficiaries under Targeted
Public Distribution System for the purpose
of National Food Security Bill; and
(b) if so, the response from State
Governments alongwith details thereof?
Drip and sprinkler irrigation
*25. SHRI R.C. SINGH: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that drip and
sprinkler irrigation is rapidly gaining ground
in the country;
(b) if so, the number of hectares covered
under drip irrigation in the State of West
Bengal, district-wise; and
(c) the details of Central subsidy
provided to farmers who adopted drip
irrigation in the State of West Bengal in the
last three years, year-wise?
Ragging incidents in NCR colleges
*26. SHRI AMAR SINGH: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number
of ragging incidents have taken place during
the current year in NCR colleges;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action Government has taken
against the Principals of those colleges and
students found involved in those
incidents?
Suicide by farmers
†*27. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is an increase in the
incidents of suicides and self-immolations
by farmers in different parts of the country
despite the rehabilitation package being in
place;
(b) if so, the number of such incidents
reported during the last two years and
till now in the current year, State-wise;
and
(c) the corrective steps taken by
Government to tackle this problem?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

10
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Agreement with State Electricity Boards
for payment of electricity charges
*28. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether her Ministry has entered
into any agreement with the State
Electricity Boards for payment of
electricity charges for plying electric trains;
(b) if so, the State Electricity Board,
which has been paid the highest rate of
electricity charges;
(c) the State Electricity Board, which
has been paid the lowest rate of electricity
charges; and
(d) the position of Kerala regarding the
rate of electricity charges?
Fresh BPL census
*29. SHRI N. BALAGANGA: Will the
Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is planning a
fresh BPL census to identify the BPL
families; and
(b) if so, the parameters proposed to be
used to identify those families?
Recent train accidents in the country
*30. SHRI VIJAY JAW AHARLAL
DARDA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether her Ministry has taken
seriously recent train accidents in the
country;
(b) if so, whether she has taken a serious
note of recent incident of Goa Express that
rammed into another train near Mathura;
(c) if so, the number of railway officials
and others who were involved in this
incident;
(d) how many officials responsible for
this have so far been dismissed and inquiry
started; and
(e) the safety measures her Ministry
has taken so far and to what extent these
measures would help avoid train accidents
in the country?
Foodgrains destroyed by rats and
insects
†*31. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) the quantum of foodgrains destroyed
by rats and insects during last three years;
(b) whether insecticides are used in
storing the foodgrains to save them from
perishing;
(c) if so, the quantum of insecticides
used each year in the last three years and
the cost incurred thereon; and
(d) the reasons for substantial loss to
the foodgrains by rats and insects despite
their upkeep with the use of insecticides?
Financial assistance from Sugar
Development Fund
*32. SHRI RAJEEV
CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister
of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Karnataka
Government has recommended nine
proposals to the Centre for financial

11
assistance from Sugar Development Fund
for the development of sugarcane areas of
the sugar factories and also for expansion-
cum-cooperation scheme; and
(b) if so, by when the proposals are
likely to be cleared by the Centre and the
reasons for delay as eight of the nine
proposals have been pending since 2002
onwards and in the ninth case in which
first instalment of assistance was released
in April, 2006, the second one is awaited
since then?
Flood and drought relief
*33. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) the estimates of aid sought by various
States at the end of this year's monsoon
season for flood and drought relief;
(b) the details of such requests actually
accepted by the Centre, State-wise;
(c) the details of cash and non-cash
components of such aid, State-wise; and
(d) the details of loans and grants
components of the aid, State-wise?
Grading system in CBSE
*34. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK: Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether grading system for
examinations is proposed to be introduced
at the Central Board of Secondary
Education (CBSE) from 2010;
(b) whether any decision has been taken
in this regard and the authorities vested
with powers to take such decisions;
(c) whether any other Education Board
has decided to introduce such grading
system and if so, the names of such Boards;
(d) whether any comparative advantage
of grading system with marks system has
been assessed by his Ministry or
Institutions attached to his Ministry or
otherwise; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Unmanned railway level crossings
*35. DR. JANARDHAN
WAGHMARE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a speeding Gonda-Ayodhya
passenger train rammed into a truck at an
unmanned level crossing on 1st November,
2009 resulting in deaths of several persons;
(b) if so, whether a large number of
unmanned railway level crossings still exist
which are posing danger to the crossing
vehicles, etc.;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government had earlier
given assurance that all unmanned railway
level crossings would be either manned or
electronic devices would be placed for
controlling vehicles, etc.; and
(e) if so, the reasons for not following
the earlier orders in this regard?
Effects of monsoon deficiency
*36. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether due to 28 per cent deficiency
in monsoon and less sown area under paddy,
oilseeds and sugarcane lower than last year,

12
kharif foodgrains production is expected
to fall sharply;
(b) if so, whether according to experts,
the loss of about 6 million hectares in paddy
sowing in the rainfed States and mortality
of standing crops in 141 drought affected
districts, would hit output severely;
(c) whether PM had also held
discussions with CMs on this issue; and
(d) if so, whether Government has taken
a policy decision as to how to address the
drought?
Construction of coach factory at
Palakkad in Kerala
*37. SHRI T.K. RANGARAJAN: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of the present status of
construction of a  coach factory at Palakkad
in Kerala;
(b) the details of the requirement of
funds and the details of funds allocated by
her Ministry towards the project;
(c) whether the initial modalities have
been completed in this regard;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) by when the work on the project is
expected to commence?
Enrolment in higher education
†*38. DR. GY AN PRAKASH
PILANIA:
SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of proposed Central
Universities, Indian Institute of Technology,
Indian Institutes of Management, Indian
Institutes of Science Education and
Research, Indian Institutes of Information
Technology, Schools and Colleges of
Planning and Architecture to be opened for
additional five per cent enrolment in higher
education during the Eleventh Five-Year
Plan period, year-wise and State-wise;
(b) the names and number of institutes
therefrom to be in Government sector,
aided sector and private sector, State-wise;
(c) the provision made by the Central
Government and State Governments,
institute-wise, amount-wise; and
(d) the increase in enrolment resulting
therefrom, State-wise?
Maintenance of record of reservation
requisition
*39. SHRI   NAND   KISHORE
YADAV:
SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to refer to answer to Unstarred
Question 3786 given in the Rajya Sabha on
7th August, 2009 and state:
(a) whether as per orders issued by
her Ministry  vide  letter No. 94/TG-1/
20/P/8, dated 2nd August, 1994 and
98/TG-1/14/P dated 23rd April, 1998
regarding preservation and maintenance
of reservation requisitions and release of
emergency/HOR quota for waitlisted
tickets, all zones, divisions and HQ
should maintain proper records in this
regard;
(b) whether these orders are not
followed properly by Railways;
(c) if so, the reasons for violation of its
own orders; and

(d) of Unstarred Question 3786 while

Improvement in primary education
*40. DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMA A.
HEPTULLA: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
India ranks woefully at 101st place in the
Global Competitive Index due to poor
primary education in the country;
(b) whether Government is also aware
that due to poor quality of primary
education, the economic competitiveness
is also being affected;
(c) if so, the action taken by Government
to improve primary education in the
country and the infrastructure in this regard;
and
(d) the steps taken to arrest the drop-
out rate and bring uniform syllabus for the
entire country?
